pageCache.pageTitle: North Lancing Primary School  Home - North Lancing Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to North Lancing Primary School
This website will give you an insight into our school and the many wonderful experiences and opportunities our pupils enjoy.
At North Lancing Primary School, we provide a happy, caring and inclusive environment where every child feels valued, supported and able to reach their full potential. We strive to create a safe and welcoming school where children can thrive, develop confidence and become the very best version of themselves.
We believe strong relationships between home and school are fundamental to children’s success. We build these through trust, shared knowledge, open communication and mutual respect.
Our school values underpin everything we do: independence, collaboration, resilience, perseverance and individuality. Our golden value, kindness, threads through all our values and shapes the way we learn, work, and grow together.
These values help our pupils to grow as learners and as kind, confident and capable young people.
If there is ever anything you would like to discuss with me, please do not hesitate to get in touch. I am always happy to listen and arrange an appointment where helpful.
Emma Brown, Headteacher

School Clubs
Benefits of joining a club
North Lancing Primary School offer a large range of different clubs. There are huge befits to taking part in extra curricular activities. These include:
Finding new interests
Building self-esteem
Increasing social opportunities
Making new friends
Improving communication skills
Providing physical and mental health benefits
Club Choice
Most staff at North Lancing run a school club. In addition, external providers offer additional opportunities for pupils to find an activity they would enjoy. School run clubs have a small charge (£5 a term) but are free for any pupils eligible for pupil premium. Clubs can include the following, but do change every term so please see the up-to-date clubs list sent out at the beginning of each term:

Wrap Around Care
Breakfast Buddies
Breakfast club runs from 7.45am until the start of the school day. It is run by a private company. A healthy breakfast and play opportunities will set your child up for the perfect start to their school day. Places can be booked by contacting hellobreakfastbuddies@gmail.com
Timing: 7.45am – 8.35am
Stay and Play
Stay and Play is our staff run after school club. It offers relaxed childcare until 6pm each day. Your child will be offered light snacks and a drink and plenty of opportunities to spend fun filled time with their friends. Places can be booked via the school office or stayandplay@northlancing.co.uk
Timing: 3pm – 6pm (5pm collection also available)

pageCache.pageTitle: North Lancing Primary School  Attendance - North Lancing Primary School
pageCache.text:
Attendance
Attendance Matters . . . Punctual and regular school attendance is an essential requirement for successful learning from the time a child starts school. We have high expectations for all our children at North Lancing Primary School. Attendance must be a priority as we can only teach those who attend. Our attendance ‘floor target’ is 96%, but we hope for 100%. Children should be at school, on time, every day the school is open unless the reason for the absence is unavoidable. There are 190 school days in each academic year. This means, 175 days in each year are non-school days. These 175 days are available to spend on family time such as visits, holidays, shopping, household jobs and other appointments.
Systems for Supporting Attendance at North Lancing

pageCache.pageTitle: North Lancing Primary School  Our School Day - North Lancing Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our School Day
Our school opening hours are:
Year R to Year 3: 8.35am to 3.00pm (Total hours a week: 32 hours 05 minutes)
Year 4 to Year 6: 8.35am to 3.05pm (Total hours a week: 32 hours 30 minutes)
Children in Reception to Year 3 should be accompanied onto the playground and parents should drop them at the classroom door. They can arrive at school any time from 8.35am and should be in class for registration at 8.45am.
At 3pm, Reception to Year 3 pupils must be collected by parents (or other named adults) from the playground near the classroom doors.
Children in Year 4 to Year 6 can arrive at school from 8.35am. Registration is at 8.45am. Their finish time is 3.05pm.
If for any reason Reception and KS1 children are not collected they are taken to the school office. Older pupils should also return to the office and notify staff that they have not been collected. A telephone call would be appreciated if parents are unavoidably delayed. Children will be looked after until collected.

pageCache.pageTitle: North Lancing Primary School  Our School Uniform - North Lancing Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our School Uniform
North Lancing Uniform
A school uniform dress code is implemented at North Lancing as it is felt that wearing matching clothing helps students feel connected to their group of peers and a part of the school community. The number of school branded items has been reduced to decrease cost. Uniform adaptions can be made for pupils with sensory needs. These can be discussed with the reception office or SEND team.
Early Years (Reception) Uniform
School logo navy sweatshirt*
White polo shirt
Grey/black/white socks
Black school shoes
Winter Uniform
School v-neck jumper or cardigan*
Navy blue pinafore dress or
Charcoal tailored trousers
White shirt (not polo shirt)
School tie*
Black/grey/white socks or navy tights
Summer Uniform
School v-neck jumper or cardigan*
Navy skirt (see winter) or
Charcoal grey tailored shorts/trousers
Black/grey/white socks
PE/Games Kit (Year 1 – 6)
Navy school logo t-shirt*
Navy unbranded shorts or
Navy unbranded cycling shorts (not too short)
Navy school logo hoodie*
Navy unbranded jogging bottoms or
Navy unbranded leggings
No jewellery can be worn for PE/Games
Swimming Kit
A sun-protection suit or
A costume/swim shorts (no bikins)
Flip Flops/Crocs
Towel or poncho towel
Earrings must be removed for swimming
Additional Items
School logo book bags and PE bags are available. These can be bought from First4Uniform. A water bottle should be brought to school daily. In addition, school logo beanie hats, jackets and bags are optional extras.
Hair/Make up
There should be no make-up, nail varnish, temporary tattoos or hair colours. Hair accessories should be in school uniform colours. Long hair must be tied back. No extreme hair styles. All make-up and nail varnish should be removed for school.
Jewellery
In the interests of safety only stud earrings and a small watch may be worn.
Children not complying can expect
The Senior leadership team will meet with parents where children are consistently not in the correct uniform.
To have a letter sent home
To have items confiscated for the day
Where to buy
Pupils in receipt of Pupil Premium funding can have up to three school branded items a year free of charge. The PTA also run a pre-loved uniform shop to help make uniform affordable for all. Items followed by a (*) are school branded uniform items and should be bought from First4Uniform or the pre-loved shop. Any items without a (*) are generic and can be purchased anywhere. If you would like help with uniform – please contact the school office.
All branded uniform is available for purchase from First4Uniform in Lancing town centre. Orders can also be made online.

Parent Pay
North Lancing is a cashless school. Parents are able to join ParentPay to make any school related payments. ParentPay is a secure online payment system that replaces cash payments for school meals, trips, events and activities in schools. ParentPay is easy to use, secure and protects your details. You can top up your account when you want, so you can budget money for lunches, trips and activities.
You will need to register and activate your account before being apply to pay for school items. This is a simple process. Before you can activate a ParentPay account, you will need an activation letter which we will provide. If you don’t have an activation letter, please contact the school office directly to request a copy.

pageCache.pageTitle: North Lancing Primary School  School Meals - North Lancing Primary School
pageCache.text:
School Meals
Go! Catering is our hot school meal provider who specialise in providing delicious, nutritious and filling school lunches for primary school children. All food is prepared and cooked on the day, using fresh ingredients, and will be brought to us ready to serve to the children.
Click here to register an account on the online booking system:
Every child registered for school lunches will receive a meal based on their individual dietary requirements (including allergies or intolerances), with a vegetarian alternative provided daily. To view our current menu, please visit the website:
Book School Meals
Go! Catering Menu
Universal Infant Free School Meals
Children in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 are entitled to free school meals.
Free School Meals and the Pupil Premium
Free lunches can be supplied to children whose parents are in receipt of Income Support, Income Based Job Seeker’s Allowance, support under Part VI of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999, Pension Credit, Income related Employment and Support Allowance or Child Tax Credit with assessed income below £16,190, but the necessary authorisation (with proof of receipt of benefit) has to be obtained, please ask at the reception office for details. (This information is confidential).
The number of children registered for free meals increases funding and we would very much appreciate parents registering their entitlement to free lunches even if they do not wish their child to receive a meal. For further details, please contact the school office.
Free School Meal Application Form
Playtime snacks
Children may bring a healthy snack to school and we allow fruit, vegetables, bread sticks and rice cakes. There is a ‘no nut’ policy at school – all foods should therefore be nut free.
Children in Reception to Year 2 are provided with a free healthy snack each day.
We do encourage pupils to drink water regularly throughout the day so non-spill bottles should be brought to school daily.
Milk is available to order at www.coolmilk.com.

pageCache.text:
SEN & Disabilities
The role of the Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENCo) is highly specialist and plays an important part in ensuring that all children are able to access and enjoy their education. The role is sometimes also referred to as the Inclusion Manager.
At North Lancing Primary School, we are fortunate to have two highly experienced teachers who share responsibility for our SEN provision:
Working as a team, our SENCos coordinate support for children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) and oversee our team of teaching assistants.
Supporting every child
Our aim is to ensure that every child at North Lancing is given the support they need to thrive. We work hard to provide a stimulating, inclusive and accessible curriculum, with appropriate adaptations and additional support where needed.
We identify children who may need additional support as early as possible and work with them, their families and relevant professionals to put the right support in place.
Support may include:
Where appropriate, we also work with external professionals and services to provide additional expertise and support.
Additional or specialist teaching
Small-group or individual interventions
Targeted support programmes
Classroom adaptations and resources
Support from our teaching assistants
Specialist advice and support from external agencies
How can I raise a concern?
If you have a concern about your child’s learning, development or additional needs, please speak to your child’s class teacher in the first instance. They will work with you to understand your concerns and, where appropriate, refer your child to the relevant SENCo.
We believe that working in partnership with parents and carers is essential. By working together, we can make sure that children receive the right support at the right time and are given every opportunity to achieve, develop their independence and enjoy their time at North Lancing.

pageCache.pageTitle: North Lancing Primary School  Reading - North Lancing Primary School
pageCache.text:
Reading
Reading Scheme
Our main aim is to give the children the reading skills to be able to read independently and for enjoyment. Children in Reception to Year 2 have daily phonics and reading sessions using the Read, Write Inc scheme. Texts match the phonics they are learning.
Pupils take home Read, Write Inc book bag books. These match the phonics they are learning at school. In addition, pupils are offered a range of supplementary texts to take home to broaden their reading. These include titles for Oxford Reading Tree, Rigby Rockets and Collins Big Cat.
Pupils who struggle with reading are supported through interventions such as FFT and Reading Eggs schemes. We also offer the Dyslexia friendly ‘Nessy’ reading programme daily for pupils with dyslexia tendencies.
In Years 3 to Year 6, North Lancing use ‘Accelerated Reader’ to help students to select appropriate reading materials, assess progress and identify areas of reading to improve. As school, pupils have read over 150 millions words a year for the past three years! AR bookfinder is an excellent resource when selecting texts: http://arbookfinder.co.uk
The most important factor, however, in children’s progress in reading is the support of parents and carers so please encourage your child to read daily at home. Together we can make a difference.

Safeguarding
Safeguarding Statement
North Lancing Primary School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. The governing body has a duty of care to pupils and all members of the school community. We have a number of policies and procedures in place that contribute to our safeguarding commitment, including our Child Protection Policy which can be viewed in the Policies section of our website and are also available upon request from the school office.
Our designated member of staff for Child Protection and Safeguarding is Mrs Emma Brown, Headteacher. You can contact her on 01903 752301. In her absence, Mrs Anneka Drummond-Davies (SENCo) or Mrs Georgina Pickford (SENCo) can deal with any safeguarding or child protection concerns on 01903 752301. Our governor with responsibility for Safeguarding is Mrs Kelly Marchie.
